prototypes.name: Classic polished
prototypes.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity visual prototype of the TDL task-list addon window for World of Warcraft: Forever.
Primary request: redesign the existing task-list window to feel polished, readable and practical during gameplay. The reference image shows the current UI, use it only for understanding existing functions; create a new visual design.
Composition: one complete front-facing floating addon window, all four edges visible, centered and filling 85% of a landscape image, neutral dark charcoal outside the window. No perspective, no device, no website, no game screenshot, no watermark, no explanatory text outside the window.
Function constraints: a SINGLE vertically scrolling task list; checkboxes at left; an unobtrusive but visible Delete action on every task; one long expanded task with a small collapse chevron; compact close X at upper right; fixed New task input and Add button at bottom. No tabs, categories, filters, dates, priorities, currencies, progress bar, sidebar or invented functions. Task text clearly legible, large enough for gameplay. Completed task uses muted green and checked box, others cream text. Spacious enough to read but avoid giant wasted empty areas. Quiet backgrounds never compete with text.
Text, exactly in English: window header "TDL", subtitle "My tasks"; task 1 "Visit the profession trainer" checked; task 2 "Gather materials for crafting" unchecked; task 3 "Plan a dungeon run with friends" unchecked and expanded, second line "Bring potions and repair your gear." as part of that same task; task 4 "Finish the quests in Westfall" unchecked; action on each row "Delete"; footer label "New task"; empty input; button "Add". Small footer hint "Double-click a task to edit".
Design direction: Classic polished. A refined Warcraft-native window with dark stone and leather panels, restrained brushed bronze frame, very thin warm gold dividers, simple centered header with a tiny checklist emblem, burgundy beveled Add button, recognizable native checkbox and scrollbar. Remove the large weapon illustration and heavy texture from behind text. Narrow elegant borders and consistent padding. Warm cream fantasy game typography. Delete buttons small and subdued, never dominating the task label. Maintain approximately a 600 by 480 window proportion. This should look like a believable improved native addon, not ornate fantasy concept art.

prototypes.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity visual prototype of the TDL task-list addon window for World of Warcraft: Forever.
Primary request: redesign the existing task-list window to feel polished, readable and practical during gameplay. The reference image shows the current UI, use it only for understanding existing functions; create a new visual design.
Composition: one complete front-facing floating addon window, all four edges visible, centered and filling 85% of a landscape image, neutral dark charcoal outside the window. No perspective, no device, no website, no game screenshot, no watermark, no explanatory text outside the window.
Function constraints: a SINGLE vertically scrolling task list; checkboxes at left; an unobtrusive but visible Delete action on every task; one long expanded task with a small collapse chevron; compact close X at upper right; fixed New task input and Add button at bottom. No tabs, categories, filters, dates, priorities, currencies, progress bar, sidebar or invented functions. Task text clearly legible, large enough for gameplay. Completed task uses muted green and checked box, others cream text. Spacious enough to read but avoid giant wasted empty areas. Quiet backgrounds never compete with text.

Design direction: Compact. A sleek compact Warcraft addon with a narrow portrait-ish 420 by 480 window, dark matte slate panels, slim bronze outline, almost flat clean surfaces, restrained warm gold heading and accent, crisp readable game UI font. Dense but comfortably padded rows, each task with compact checkbox at left and small visible Delete action tucked under its right side. Expanded task uses only two lines. Thin scrollbar at right. Title aligned left with a tiny bronze checklist emblem, close X right. Clearly spaced footer with New task, long input and small gold-accent Add button. High-end understated dark game utility, retaining a medieval visual hint through border and lettering. Not a web SaaS dashboard. Avoid rounded cards, neon, excessive ornament, excessive blank height.
prototypes.refinement: Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the reference TDL window into a genuinely compact modern game utility. Keep the same four task texts, completion state, expanded second line, one scrollbar, New task input, Add and close X, and hint. Change only visual layout and styling. DRAMATICALLY reduce window height by removing all blank space below task 4, footer starts immediately after task 4. Header should be a SINGLE low 40px strip reading "TDL · My tasks", with a small 18px checklist icon, NOT a large two-line title block. Reduce row padding to 12px. Replace all four big red Delete buttons with small subdued readable text-only "Delete" actions at the right; no red fill or bevel on them. Replace chunky 3D checkboxes with simple square bronze outlined checkboxes with a small green tick for completed task. Add button should be small, matte dark bronze with light text, not red. Plain flat dark slate surface, no leather or stone textures, remove ornate corner fittings, no cards around each task: only fine horizontal separators. Thin straight bronze border. Clean crisp sans-serif game typography. The resulting entire window should be about 460px wide and 360px tall, viewed frontally with all edges visible, on neutral charcoal backdrop. A clear distinct more understated compact option than native ornamented Warcraft UI. No new features, tabs, filters or labels.

revisions.name: Classic revised towards GuildStock
revisions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: revised visual prototype of the TDL World of Warcraft: Forever addon window.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, original classic TDL concept. Image 2 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, GuildStock. The user asks to tone down the classic ornament and make TDL feel part of the same family as GuildStock.
Primary request: redesign Image 1's visuals towards GuildStock's restrained modern fantasy addon aesthetic. Preserve all TDL functions and the same four sample tasks, completion state, one expanded task, single scrollbar and bottom input with Add.
Visual changes: remove heavy carved stone and leather textures, corner armor and rivets, large central raised title plaque, thick embossed shiny gold and big red Delete buttons. Use smooth near-black warm brown surfaces with flat slightly lighter dark brown panels; extremely thin muted bronze gold outer border and dividers. GuildStock current palette: window #18130B, panels #201A0F, header #291F0F, borders #59452B, bronze #A3763B, cream #F0E0BA, body text #D4C7AB. Quiet background. Small restrained bronze corners, no heavy ornament. Header left aligned like GuildStock: small checklist icon followed by cream serif "TDL", smaller muted subtitle "My tasks", with a native compact close X at upper right. Header roughly 65px high at 600px window width. Body text clean readable game sans-serif like GuildStock; reserve serif for title only. Rows on one continuous panel separated by thin faint lines, no separate boxed cards. Moderate row heights. Completed text muted green with checked square, all others warm cream. Delete actions small plain dark buttons or text with very subtle border and muted label, not red. Add button flat warm dark brown with fine gold border and cream text. Slim unobtrusive bronze scrollbar. Footer compact with clear New task label, empty input, Add button and small muted editing hint. Window proportions roughly 600x460, neutral dark background outside, front facing, all edges visible, window fills most of image.
Text verbatim: "TDL", "My tasks", "Visit the profession trainer", "Gather materials for crafting", "Plan a dungeon run with friends", "Bring potions and repair your gear.", "Finish the quests in Westfall", "Delete" on each task, "New task", "Add", "Double-click a task to edit".
Constraints: only ONE TDL window. Do not copy GuildStock's columns, tabs, sidebar, player names, materials, search, inventory, guild functions or labels. No new features, no progress, no categories, no watermark or captions outside window. Keep recognizably Warcraft but polished and less ornate, not a generic web dashboard.
